claims.claim: ChatGPT violated the one-page ruleset's two core mechanics within the first turns (no complication after a success, arithmetic wrong on the target number).
claims.source: The Alexandrian — Thought of the Day: GenAI and RPGs (Justin Alexander, 2025-12-28)
claims.page: The Alexandrian — Thought of the Day: GenAI and RPGs (Justin Alexander, 2025-12-28)

claims.claim: Read-aloud announces 'the desperate cry of a woman in distress' and that a mask 'emanates a palpable malevolence' instead of letting players feel it.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — The Curse of the Swamp (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-01, plus comments)
claims.quote: You're telling people things. You want to SHOW people things.
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — The Curse of the Swamp (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-01, plus comments)

claims.claim: Commenters flagged the prose as AI or EASL and the publisher's reply as written in ChatGPT style; hooks were 'standard please help me stuff, very abstract'.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — The Curse of the Swamp (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-01, plus comments)
claims.quote: the prose reeks of either EASL or AI
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — The Curse of the Swamp (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-01, plus comments)

claims.claim: Room openers like 'Arriving at the house, the PCs see a strange sight: the structure appears to be…' say nothing and can be deleted without impact; every encounter does this.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — A Strange House (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-11-25, plus comments)
claims.quote: Note the padding. Note how it doesn't say ANYTHING.
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — A Strange House (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-11-25, plus comments)

claims.claim: A commenter identifies the padding as ChatGPT's default when asked to 'write a room description for a D&D game'; 'be brief' removes it, but the author must first see it as meaningless.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — A Strange House (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-11-25, plus comments)
claims.quote: A tell-tale sign of ChatGPT, btw. It's its default style
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — A Strange House (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-11-25, plus comments)

claims.claim: Commenters note the model's style inherits the mediocrity of the typical D&D adventure writing it was trained on.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — A Strange House (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-11-25, plus comments)
claims.quote: the typical D&D adventure writing ChatGPT was trained on
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — A Strange House (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-11-25, plus comments)

claims.claim: The review contrasts the module's weak abstract adjectives with the concrete detail a good description needs.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — A Strange House (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-11-25, plus comments)
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — A Strange House (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-11-25, plus comments)

claims.claim: The intro read-aloud is full of second-person narration of the players' own actions, which a commenter attributes to ChatGPT's default unless told 'not to describe my actions'.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — A Plague of Rats (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-08, plus comments)
claims.quote: YOU step off the boat. YOU see a so and so.
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — A Plague of Rats (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-08, plus comments)

claims.claim: A commenter received the module's exact corridor phrase from ChatGPT a year earlier for a different sewer adventure — same prompt, same output.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — A Plague of Rats (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-08, plus comments)
claims.quote: the results will be almost or exactly the same
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — A Plague of Rats (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-08, plus comments)

claims.claim: No typographic distinction between read-aloud and DM text; the long intro diverts player attention.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — A Plague of Rats (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-08, plus comments)
claims.quote: It just sort of all runs together
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — A Plague of Rats (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-08, plus comments)

claims.claim: The module's 'stench of decay… dripping water echoes off the damp walls' line is cited as the predictable generated sensory opener; three dock encounters reuse identical read-aloud.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — A Plague of Rats (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-08, plus comments)
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — A Plague of Rats (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-06-08, plus comments)

claims.claim: Everything in the module gets a backstory and the read-aloud reveals all details, so players need not engage in the back-and-forth that is the heart of play; a commenter asks whether the publisher relies on AI.
claims.source: tenfootpole.org — The Temple of the Serpent Queen (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-08-07, plus comments)
claims.page: tenfootpole.org — The Temple of the Serpent Queen (Bryce Lynch review, 2024-08-07, plus comments)

claims.claim: ChatGPT's explanations are superficially plausible technobabble that get less clear on inspection because it is generating plausible word-sequences with no idea what they mean.
claims.source: tenfootpole forum — Making a Module using ChatGPT, page 4 (Dec 2022)
claims.page: tenfootpole forum — Making a Module using ChatGPT, page 4 (Dec 2022)

claims.claim: Generated rooms had trap doors in the ceiling that characters fall through; the bot does not understand up and down.
claims.source: tenfootpole forum — Making a Module using ChatGPT, page 4 (Dec 2022)
claims.quote: does not understand the implications of “up” and “down”
claims.page: tenfootpole forum — Making a Module using ChatGPT, page 4 (Dec 2022)

claims.claim: A generated 'burst of flame' had no damage stats — pure fluff with no game effect.
claims.source: tenfootpole forum — Making a Module using ChatGPT, page 4 (Dec 2022)
claims.quote: it's pure fluff with no effect
claims.page: tenfootpole forum — Making a Module using ChatGPT, page 4 (Dec 2022)
